steps.title: Recognize the long and short forms
steps.body: The retained но́вый and нов both mean new. The first is the long form and the second is the masculine singular short form. The grammatical check asks which form is shown, rather than its English gloss. Long adjectives have case, gender and number inflection; short adjectives vary for gender and number, not case. The retained examples are recognition targets, not a universal rule for producing short forms by removing endings.

steps.title: Distinguish a predicate from a noun description
steps.body: In the taught modern use, short adjectives occur only in the nominative and are used predicatively to describe their subject. A long adjective often describes a noun attributively and can also be a predicate. The choice depends on the sentence, not a universal rule about one fixed word position. The isolated pair does not provide a complete context for selecting every long-versus-short form; broader agreement and sentence-level application remain pending.

steps.title: A short-looking word need not be a short adjective
steps.body: The retained беж means beige and is an invariant colour form, unchanged for case, gender and number. Its short appearance does not make it the short counterpart of но́вый. Keep lexical meaning, inflection and adjective function separate. The correct glosses remain in Vocabulary Lab as word-meaning practice; they do not satisfy the independent adjective grammar checks.

steps.body: The complete clauses Поезд старый and Студент новый say that the train is old and the student is new. Their long adjectives predicate a property of the subject. steps.title: Distinguish a noun phrase from a predication
steps.body: The supplied новый карандаш and новое письмо mean new pencil and new letter. Each is an attributive noun phrase: the adjective modifies the head noun. The complete clauses Поезд старый and Студент новый say that the train is old and the student is new. Their long adjectives predicate a property of the subject. No overt present copula appears in these supplied clauses. Long form therefore does not force attributive function, and a temporary-versus-permanent slogan does not decide every form choice. Read the whole example and its supplied meaning rather than its adjective ending alone.

The supplied новый карандаш and новое письмо mean new pencil and new letter. Each is an attributive noun phrase: the adjective modifies the head noun. These phrases alone do not assert that a pencil or letter is new in a complete clause. The adjective and noun agree in gender and number in the supplied singular examples. Do not infer an exceptionless word-position rule or every possible case from an isolated phrase. These exercises assess bounded agreement and function recognition, not unrestricted production or every long/short meaning distinction.
